Summary from discovery call: CTO (Maya Patel) worried about sudden traffic spikes during promotional campaigns - 'we see 10x traffic for ~10 minutes, and 429s cause ticket volume to spike'
- Current setup: webhooks -> support-queue -> server-side batching -> calls to hosted_api (chat completions).
- Observed behavior during POC: 429s at ~150 concurrent reqs, p95 latency climbs, retry storms from frontend led to more 429s.
- Requirements voiced:
  * P99 latency target: < 500ms for single-turn chat during normal load; willing to accept higher in extreme bursts.
  * Concurrency target: baseline 20-30 concurrent requests, must withstand short bursts to 200 reqs for 5-10 minutes during promotions.
  * Cost sensitivity: SMB budget, wants guidance on batching + lower-cost model fallbacks when appropriate.
  * Monitoring + alerts: needs token-level cost dashboard and 429 alerting to ops (Slack/Gmail).
- Quote from CTO: 'If a sale causes the bot to go offline for 10 minutes, we lose thousands in orders and escalate tickets. We need graceful degradation not hard failures.'
- Action items: send sample rate-limit headers and client retry library snippets, propose a canary policy and burst allowance with automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant, share cost-estimate for expected traffic profile.
traffic_profile: Baseline: ~25 concurrent chat requests (50k tokens/day). Peak: flash-sale spikes to ~150-200 concurrent reqs for 5-10 minutes (authored by marketing). Typical message size: 80-200 tokens. Wants 50-200 req/s burst allowance with automated short-term capacity; expects 429 handling and informative Retry-After headers.
model_preferences: Prefer lower-latency small/medium open models for chat in production; want optional fallback to quantized variants for cost during bursts. Interested in Redwood's model catalog suggestions and verified perf profiles.
